runs.text: Kuwait, judged like Israel. Ready? The test: the same apartheid definition used on Israel. Kuwait has more than one hundred thousand stateless Bidun. Many families have lived there for generations. Some served in its army and police. Citizenship? Denied. Birth and marriage certificates? Withheld. Most jobs? Closed. Free government schools? Most Bidun children can't attend. Kuwait says many are hiding another nationality. By the same definition used on Israel: is this apartheid? You decide. Israel: one in five citizens is Arab. They vote. Arab parties won nineteen seats. Arab judges sit on the Supreme Court. Kuwait is rarely called apartheid. Israel is called it daily. Both have real problems. One standard. So, let's run the test again.
